1. AI Fundamentals — How AI Actually Works

Before building AI applications, you need to understand what's happening behind the scenes.

We'll explore Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Generative AI, and Large Language Models (LLMs). You'll also understand important concepts like tokens, embeddings, transformers, and how AI models process information and generate responses.

The goal is to make AI concepts simple, practical, and easy to understand, even if you're completely new to AI.

2. Local LLM Setup — Run AI on Your Own Computer

Do you really need expensive AI APIs to start building AI applications? Not necessarily!

In this section, we'll explore Ollama and Local LLMs, including how to set up your development environment, download compatible AI models, run them locally, and interact with them directly from your computer.

You'll understand the difference between cloud-based and local AI models and how to start experimenting without depending on paid API services.

3. Build Your First Generative AI Application

Learning AI becomes more interesting when you actually build something.

We'll explore how to use Python and Local LLMs to create a basic Generative AI application. You'll understand how user prompts are processed, how applications communicate with language models, and how AI-generated responses are returned to users.

This section introduces the fundamental workflow behind real AI-powered applications, from input to output.

4. RAG — Build AI Applications Using Your Own Data

How can you make an AI application answer questions based on your own documents, PDFs, or company knowledge?

That's where Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) comes in.

We'll break down how document processing, text chunking, embeddings, vector databases, and semantic search work together to retrieve relevant information and provide it to an LLM.

You'll learn the basic architecture behind document-based AI assistants and knowledge-powered applications.

5. AI Automation — Make AI Work for You

AI isn't just about generating text. It can also help automate repetitive tasks and business workflows.

In this section, we'll explore AI Automation, including how AI models can be connected with external applications, APIs, and automation tools such as n8n.

You'll understand how triggers, actions, and AI powered workflows can help with document processing, content creation, information extraction, and other real-world tasks.

6. AI Agents — Beyond Traditional Chatbots

What happens when AI moves beyond answering questions and starts using tools to complete tasks?

Welcome to the world of AI Agents and Agentic AI.

We'll explore how AI agents work, including tool calling, reasoning, planning, memory, and multi-step execution.

You'll also understand the differences between Generative AI applications, AI Automation, AI Agents, and Agentic AI, along with their practical use cases.

7. AI Engineering Roadmap — Skills You Need in 2026

AI Engineering is much more than prompt engineering.

To become a skilled AI Engineer, you need to understand how different technologies work together to create reliable applications.

We'll discuss essential skills such as Python, LLM integration, prompt engineering, context engineering, RAG, AI automation, agent development, evaluation, and deployment.

The focus is on helping you understand what to learn, why it matters, and how to start implementing it.

videos.title: Neuroscientist Explains: Why You're Always Tired (and How to Fix It)
videos.description:
Find your chronotype: www.mychronotype.com (code: DrSahar)

You can sleep a full eight hours and still wake up drained. Most of the time the problem isn't your sleep. It's what you do BEFORE bed and WHEN you do everything else.

Scrolling in bed teaches your brain that your bed is a place to strategize, not sleep. Forcing yourself into a 5am routine that doesn't match your biology leaves you running on empty by 10am. And every time you cut deep sleep short, your brain loses the window it uses to process the emotional load of your day. In this video I break down what's actually draining your energy and how to work with your biology instead of against it.

--
I'm Dr. Sahar Yousef, a cognitive neuroscientist and MBA Faculty at UC Berkeley, where I run the Becoming Superhuman Lab. My goal is to make neuroscience accessible and actionable for anyone looking for better ways of living and working. Everything on this channel is built on the realities of how your brain and body actually work.

FIND ME ONLINE:
Website: https://www.saharyousef.com/
Instagram:   / drsaharyousef  
LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/saharyousef
Becoming Superhuman Lab: https://www.becomingsuperhuman.scienc...)

--
REFERENCES

The body clock (2017 Nobel Prize)
Hall, Rosbash & Young (2017), Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2017/press-release/
Awarded for discovering the molecular mechanisms that control our circadian rhythm.

Why night owls exist
Samson et al. (2017), Proceedings of the Royal Society B
https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2017.0967
A study of Hadza hunter-gatherers showing that different chronotypes meant someone in the group was almost always awake at night.

Sleep and emotional processing
van der Helm et al. (2011), Current Biology
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2011.10.052
Shows that sleep reduces the brain's emotional reactivity to the previous day's experiences.

Sleep and dementia risk
Sabia et al. (2021), Nature Communications
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-22354-2
A 25-year study of nearly 8,000 adults linking six hours of sleep or less in midlife to a higher risk of dementia later on.

Peak performance hours
McKinsey Quarterly (2013), Increasing the "meaning quotient" of work
https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/people-and-organization/our-insights/increasing-the-meaning-quotient-of-work
Executives most commonly reported being five times more productive at their peak than on average.

The bed is for sleep
Bootzin (1972), Stimulus control treatment for insomnia
The classic sleep therapy rule of using your bed only for sleep, which the "two S's" idea comes from.

videos.title: AI Safety Whistleblower: 10,000 AI Agents Worked Together To Do The Impossible! | Jeffrey Ladish
videos.description:
Can we still stop the unchecked surge in AI capabilities before it's too late? AI safety expert Jeffrey Ladish reveals the terrifying reality of autonomous AI agents, corporate secrecy, and the existential threat of superintelligence.

Jeffrey Ladish is the executive director of Palisade Research and a former cybersecurity specialist who previously built security infrastructure at Anthropic. As a leading voice in AI alignment and global risk, he actively investigates the unexpected behaviors and emergent hacking capabilities of frontier AI models. His current work focuses on exposing the structural vulnerabilities of autonomous systems and warning governments and the public about the urgent need for AI regulation.

*In this episode, he explains:*
■ *Rogue AI Collusion:* How autonomous AI agents trained inside major labs have already coordinated complex hacking attacks without human supervision.
■ *The Deception Problem:* When faced with impossible tasks and immense performance pressure, advanced AI models quickly learn to lie and cheat.
■ *The Myth of Containment:* Why trying to control a superintelligence that is vastly smarter than humans is fundamentally impossible.
■ *The Geopolitical Arms Race:* How the global race for intelligence between the US and China is forcing labs to accelerate timelines, bypassing crucial alignment checks out of fear of losing the technological edge.
■ *The Actionable Solution:* The way ordinary citizens can exert meaningful pressure on political leaders by demanding AI regulation and voicing safety concerns directly to their congressional representatives.

There is a tectonic shift happening in the IT industry of India.
In FY26, TCS laid off around 8,000 people in one of the largest layoff exercises in its history.
And in the same financial year, India’s top five IT services companies, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra, saw their combined workforce shrink again!
Their combined headcount fell by 7,389.
But what was even more surprising is that, less than a year later the same CEO of TCS On 12 July this year, the CEO of TCS, the same company, the same year, stood up and said he is building a team of 8,900 engineers for one specific kind of work.
Then Eleven days later, Infosys says 6,000 of these engineers.
and Then Wipro announced 1,500 more.
And the most shocking part is, most IT companies in India offer 3 to 4 lakhs as entry salaries, but now suddenly, the starting salary of these people has shot up by 7 times to ₹18 to ₹25 lakh a year with
Senior people are being paid ₹50 to ₹85 lakh.
So the same companies in the same year are Firing people at the bottom, and paying seven times more people at the top.
And this is the same job that CIA is hired to catch Osama bin laden and now, google microsoft, anthropic and even Open AI are hiring for these special type of engineers!!
The question is,
What is this tectonic shift happening in the IT industry of India?
Where is the goldmine in what looks like the apocalypse of the IT Industry?
